wp:category.wp:category_description: Educational and commercial insights about aerogel materials, insulation technologies, suppliers, and industrial applications.

wp:term.wp:term_description: Aerogel Insulation Blankets are high-performance composite materials engineered by impregnating aerogel into flexible fibrous matrices, such as glass fiber, pre-oxidized carbon fiber, or ceramic fiber. As the most commercially mature form of aerogel, these blankets combine the ultra-low thermal conductivity of silica aerogel with the mechanical strength of textile fibers. They offer superior thermal protection in a significantly thinner profile compared to traditional insulation (like rock wool or PIR), making them the gold standard for industrial piping, oil and gas facilities, and architectural energy-saving projects. Their hydrophobic nature and high durability ensure long-term performance even in harsh, humid environments.

Aerogel Powder and Granules represent the fundamental high-porosity form of aerogel material, featuring an internal structure that is over 95% air. These particles are primarily utilized as high-performance functional additives across various industries. Available in micron-sized powders or millimeter-sized granules, they can be integrated into specialized coatings, thermal renders, and advanced plastic composites to drastically reduce heat transfer. In the manufacturing sector, these materials are favored for their exceptional surface area and versatility, allowing for the creation of "super-insulating" paints and slurries that can be applied to complex geometries where traditional blankets cannot reach.
Manufacturers producing silica aerogel, aerogel blankets, and related thermal insulation materials.

Specifically designed for the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) and Energy Storage System (ESS) markets, Aerogel Battery Thermal Pads are precision-engineered safety components. These pads are typically composed of thin aerogel composites reinforced with specialized flame-retardant fibers, often encapsulated in protective films to prevent dust shedding. Positioned between individual battery cells or modules, they serve as a critical thermal barrier to prevent "thermal runaway" propagation—effectively blocking heat transfer if a single cell fails. These pads are characterized by their ultra-thin profile, high compression resistance, and "Class A" fire-retardancy, ensuring the structural integrity and safety of high-density battery packs.
Distributors, traders, and channel partners supplying aerogel products across key regional markets.
Suppliers of aerogel characterization instruments, supercritical process equipment, specialty silanes, and development materials for research, pilot production, and industrial scale-up.
Research institutes, testing laboratories, and technical service providers supporting aerogel development.

item.title: Cabot Corporation - Aerogel Business
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Cabot Corporation is a leading global specialty chemicals and performance materials company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. Their aerogel division produces and markets Industrial Aerogel Insulation under the Nanogel brand. Cabot's aerogel products are used in oil and gas pipeline insulation, building and construction, industrial insulation, and unique specialty applications. Nanogel aerogel is a highly insulating, lightweight, and hydrophobic material. Cabot has been a pioneer in commercializing aerogel technology for industrial use, with manufacturing facilities in Frankfurt, Germany.
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: United States of America; Vendor: aerogel a.

item.title: Enersens (Formerly Gu techno)
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Enersens is a French company specializing in the development and manufacturing of high-performance aerogel-based insulation solutions. Formerly known as Gu techno, the company produces innovative silica aerogel materials for thermal and acoustic insulation in industrial, building, and transportation sectors. Their proprietary production process allows for cost-effective manufacturing of aerogel blankets and boards with exceptional thermal performance. Enersens serves clients across Europe and has established partnerships with major industrial groups.
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: France; Vendor: aerogel a.

item.title: JIOS Aerogel Corporation
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: JIOS Aerogel Corporation is a Singapore-based company that specializes in the development and production of aerogel materials and products. The company has developed a proprietary aerogel production technology that significantly reduces manufacturing costs while maintaining high quality standards. JIOS Aerogel produces aerogel powder, aerogel blankets, and aerogel panels for applications in oil and gas, construction, industrial insulation, and lithium-ion battery safety. The company has strategic partnerships with major energy companies and has expanded its operations to serve the Asia-Pacific market.
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: Singapore; Vendor: aerogel a.

item.title: Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. | China Aerogel Manufacturer
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. is a Chinese aerogel manufacturer founded in 2004. The company describes itself as a national high-tech enterprise integrating research, production, and sales of silica aerogel materials and aerogel composite products for industrial insulation, energy, and battery safety applications.

Company Overview

The company serves domestic and export markets with a product portfolio that spans silica aerogel insulation materials, custom thermal-protection products, and specialty composites. Its public English-language site highlights long-running aerogel R&D and commercialization activity in Zhejiang Province.

Coverage and Focus

  • Coverage Area: Mainland China and export-oriented international markets.
  • Focus Areas: Silica aerogel materials, industrial thermal insulation, battery thermal protection, and specialty aerogel composite development.

Main Products and Capacity

  • Customized battery thermal-protection products
  • Removable insulation covers
  • Aerogel fabric
  • Powders and coatings
  • Aerogel pipe shells
  • Public Capacity: Not clearly disclosed on the English pages reviewed.

Production Sites and Certifications

  • Main Production Site: Zhejiang Province, China.
  • International Certifications: Not clearly disclosed on the English pages reviewed.
  • Official Website: https://en.nanuo.cn/

FAQ

What does Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. manufacture?

Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. publicly offers Aerogel Coating & Slurry, Aerogel Insulation Blanket, Aerogel Pipe Shell & Cover, Aerogel Powder & Granules, Battery Thermal Pad / Cell-to-Cell Barrier. Buyers commonly review this listing to understand the company’s product scope, production profile, and official website information before making contact.

Where is Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. located?

Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. is listed with production or operating presence in Zhejiang Province, China.. Where more detailed plant information is publicly available, it is summarized in the Production Sites and Certifications section above.

Which industries does Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. serve?

Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. serves Building & Construction, EV Batteries & Energy Storage, Industrial Insulation, Petrochemical & Oil & Gas. The public company profile and application materials indicate a focus on thermal insulation, safety, and energy-efficiency scenarios that use aerogel-based materials.

Does Nano High-Tech Co., Ltd. publish international certifications?

Not clearly disclosed on the English pages reviewed.

item.title: Active Aerogels
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Active Aerogels is a Portuguese company focused on the development and commercialization of aerogel-based thermal insulation products. The company produces high-performance aerogel blankets and boards designed for industrial applications, including oil and gas, petrochemical, and building insulation. Active Aerogels leverages advanced sol-gel technology to produce aerogels with ultra-low thermal conductivity, excellent hydrophobicity, and long-term durability. Their products are designed to meet the demanding requirements of industrial insulation while reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions.
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: Portugal; Vendor: aerogel a.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Directory profile reviewed for listing quality, category fit, and current public website availability.

item.title: BASF SE - Aerogel Solutions
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: BASF SE, the world's largest chemical company based in Ludwigshafen, Germany, offers advanced aerogel solutions as part of its performance materials portfolio. BASF's Slentite aerogel panels are polyurethane-based aerogel insulation boards that combine excellent thermal insulation with mechanical strength and easy processing. These panels are used in building insulation, refrigeration, and industrial applications. BASF leverages its extensive chemical expertise and global research infrastructure to continuously innovate in aerogel technology, focusing on sustainability and energy efficiency.
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: Germany; Vendor: aerogel a.

item.title: Thermablok Aerogel Insulation
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Thermablok is a well-known supplier of aerogel-based insulation solutions for the building sector. The company commercializes thin-profile aerogel insulation products designed to reduce thermal bridging in residential, commercial, and retrofit construction projects.

  • Coverage Area: North America, the United Kingdom, and selected international markets
  • Focus Areas: Thermal-bridge mitigation, building-envelope upgrades, retrofit insulation, window and door interfaces, and thin-profile construction insulation
  • Current Brands Represented: Thermablok® aerogel insulation products
  • Official Website: https://www.thermablok.com

item.title: Aerogel Technologies LLC
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Aerogel Technologies LLC is a U.S. specialty company focused on custom aerogel materials, formulation development, and small-batch supply for research and industrial programs. Its portfolio includes silica aerogels, carbon aerogels, and related custom materials used in laboratory testing, prototyping, and specialty applications. The company is relevant to the Equipment Materials category as a source of development-stage aerogel materials and technical support for R&D-driven projects.

item.title: Blueshift International Materials
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Blueshift International Materials develops and manufactures polyimide aerogel materials under the brand AeroZero, producing ultra-thin, flexible aerogel films for aerospace, defense, and advanced electronics applications. Their technology enables aerogels in thin-film form factors not achievable with traditional silica aerogels. The company was founded based on technology developed at NASA.

item.title: Insulcon BV
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Insulcon BV is a Dutch thermal insulation specialist supplying high-temperature insulation systems to industrial customers across Europe and beyond. Its aerogel offering supports energy, petrochemical, process, and power-sector applications where thin and high-performance insulation is required.

  • Coverage Area: Netherlands, Europe, and international industrial markets
  • Focus Areas: High-temperature insulation, industrial process insulation, petrochemical systems, power generation, refractory applications, and aerogel blanket solutions

item.title: Armacell International S.A. | Luxembourg Aerogel Insulation Manufacturer
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Armacell International S.A. is a global insulation manufacturer whose public product messaging includes ArmaGel®, an aerogel-insulation range focused on thin-profile thermal control for demanding industrial environments. Public company materials position ArmaGel around high-performance blanket insulation for projects where space savings, hydrophobic behavior, and heat-loss control matter.

Company Overview

Armacell is widely known in the thermal and technical insulation market, and its ArmaGel line is presented as part of that broader insulation portfolio. The strongest public emphasis appears to be on industrial and energy-sector insulation rather than broad commodity building products, making the company relevant to buyers screening aerogel blanket suppliers for process equipment, piping, and retrofit work.

Coverage and Focus

  • Coverage Area: Global commercial reach through Armacell’s multinational insulation business.
  • Focus Areas: Industrial insulation, space-constrained retrofits, hydrophobic thermal insulation systems, and low-thickness solutions for demanding process environments.

Main Products and Capacity

  • Public Product Reference: ArmaGel® aerogel insulation blanket grades marketed for industrial thermal-insulation use.
  • Public Product Family Reference: Public-facing materials commonly refer to ArmaGel grades such as HT and XGH, though exact current regional availability should be confirmed directly with Armacell.
  • Public Capacity: Specific aerogel production-capacity figures are not clearly disclosed on the reviewed public company materials available to this directory workflow.

Production Sites and Certifications

  • Main Corporate Base: Luxembourg-based corporate identity with global manufacturing and insulation-market operations.
  • Supply Position: Public product messaging supports Armacell’s role as a commercial supplier of aerogel-insulation solutions through its broader insulation network.
  • Official Website: https://www.armacell.com/

FAQ

Why is Armacell included in the aerogel producer directory?

Armacell publicly markets the ArmaGel product family as aerogel insulation, making it a relevant commercial aerogel-insulation producer/supplier for industrial buyers.

What is the main ArmaGel focus?

Public product messaging most strongly emphasizes industrial thermal-insulation applications where reduced thickness, hydrophobic performance, and easier retrofit handling are valuable.

What should buyers verify directly?

Buyers should confirm exact product grade, service-temperature range, facing/jacketing options, and regional availability directly with Armacell before specification or procurement.

Certifications and Compliance represent the formal verification of a manufacturer's quality management, environmental stewardship, and product safety standards. In the aerogel industry, these credentials are indispensable for ensuring material reliability under extreme conditions. This category encompasses international management systems (such as ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and IATF 16949 for automotive supply chains) alongside rigorous material performance testing (such as ASTM, UL, and CE fire-retardancy ratings). For global buyers and engineers, these certifications serve as a critical technical filter for risk mitigation, ensuring that the aerogel products meet the stringent safety and thermal requirements of high-stakes industrial and automotive applications.

item.title: Empa — Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded: Aerogel Research Institute. Empa — Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology — is a leading public-sector materials research institution based in Dübendorf, Switzerland. Its Building Energy Materials and Concrete & Asphalt laboratories have published extensively on silica aerogel-based insulating plasters, aerogel-enhanced concrete, and aerogel blanket systems for building envelope retrofitting. Empa researchers have contributed to the development and performance evaluation of aerogel-based thermal insulation across the full value chain, from material synthesis and characterization to building physics simulation and real-world demonstration projects. The institution also operates NEST, a modular research and innovation building, where aerogel insulation products have been tested under realistic conditions. Empa's aerogel-related work is relevant for researchers, manufacturers, and building professionals seeking expertise in advanced porous insulation materials, thermal performance testing, and building integration.

item.title: Svenska Aerogel AB | Sweden Quartzene Aerogel Manufacturer
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Svenska Aerogel AB (Svenska Aerogel Holding AB, publ) is a Swedish deep-tech company that manufactures and commercializes Quartzene®, a proprietary mesoporous silica aerogel material produced via a patented waterborne process. The company positions Quartzene as a functional additive that delivers classic aerogel properties — low density, low thermal conductivity, and high absorption capacity — while using commonly available silica sources, water, and green energy in a more sustainable manufacturing process than traditional supercritical drying.

Company Overview
Svenska Aerogel is publicly traded on the Swedish market and operates a dedicated production facility in Gävle, Sweden, approximately 170 km north of Stockholm. The company's core technology is built around Quartzene, a silica-aerogel powder produced at industrial scale for incorporation into end products across multiple sectors. Svenska Aerogel also produces SeaQare, an antifouling paint composition derived from its aerogel platform.

Coverage and Focus
Coverage Area: Global commercial reach with production in Sweden and partnerships across European and international markets.
Focus Areas: Functional aerogel additives for thermal insulation coatings, building materials, EV battery thermal safety, marine antifouling, and industrial process applications.

Main Products and Capacity
Public Product Reference: Quartzene® mesoporous silica aerogel powder, marketed as a functional additive for incorporation into coatings, paints, plasters, building panels, sealants, textiles, and EV battery systems.
Public Product Family Reference: Quartzene (insulation and absorption grades) and SeaQare (antifouling paint additive).
Public Capacity: The Gävle production facility has a current annual capacity of 225 tons, with stated expansion capability to 1,000 tons per year.

Production Sites and Certifications
Main Corporate Base: Gävle, Sweden. Publicly traded parent company: Svenska Aerogel Holding AB (publ).
Supply Position: Manufacturer with proprietary patented production technology and in-house industrial-scale facility.

  • Official Website: https://aerogel.se
item.excerpt:encoded: Category: Aerogel Producers; Location: Sweden; Vendor: aerogel a.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Publicly traded Swedish aerogel manufacturer with verified official website and product documentation. Quartzene production facility confirmed.

item.title: Insulcon Group | Netherlands Aerogel Blanket Distributor
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
The Insulcon Group is a leading European distributor and converter of high-temperature insulation solutions, headquartered in Steenbergen, the Netherlands. Founded in 1980 and part of the IPCOM Group since 2015, Insulcon supplies a comprehensive range of thermal insulation products and engineered systems to industrial customers across Europe and worldwide.

Insulcon is an authorized distributor of Aspen Aerogels products, offering the full range of Pyrogel® and Cryogel® aerogel insulation blankets. These include Pyrogel® XTE for corrosion-under-insulation protection in medium-to-high temperature service, Pyrogel® XTF combining thermal insulation with passive fire protection, Pyrogel® HPS optimized for high-temperature hydrocarbon and chemical processing, and Cryogel® Z for cryogenic and sub-ambient applications down to −200 °C. Insulcon provides tailored, CNC-waterjet-cut aerogel insulation sections for pipes, elbows, valves, vessels, and other equipment.

  • Coverage Area: Europe-wide distribution with offices and facilities in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Hungary, and France; global network of dedicated agents
  • Focus Areas: High-temperature insulation, cryogenic insulation, passive fire protection, aerogel blanket distribution and conversion, petrochemical and LNG insulation, power generation insulation, marine and offshore insulation
  • Current Brands Represented: Aspen Aerogels (Pyrogel®, Cryogel®), Insulcon proprietary Calcon calcium silicate, Insulboard MPU microporous products, and additional refractory and fibre-based insulation brands
  • Official Website: www.insulcon.com

The company’s official website confirms distribution and conversion of aerogel insulation blankets across petrochemical, LNG, power generation, offshore, and industrial markets. Insulcon operates state-of-the-art CNC waterjet cutting facilities and an in-house engineering department to deliver project-specific aerogel insulation solutions, including pre-formed sections for piping and equipment, with cladding supplied as an integrated one-stop-shop offering.

This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://aerogela.com.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.title: Claim Listing
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Claim Listing

Are you the official representative of a company, supplier, distributor, laboratory, or service provider already listed on Aerogela? Use this page to request control of the existing listing instead of creating a duplicate entry.

Before you submit

  • Use a business email on your company domain whenever possible.
  • Add your company website and a proof link such as a team page, contact page, or profile page.
  • Explain your role and why you are authorized to manage the listing.

What happens next

  • Aerogela reviews your request manually.
  • Typical review time is 2–5 business days.
  • If approved, the listing can be marked as officially managed and linked to the representative account.
[aerogela_claim_listing]

item.title: Submit a Listing
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Submit a Listing

Use this page to understand how Aerogela reviews new supplier, manufacturer, distributor, laboratory, and service-provider listings before you start the actual submission form.

Submit a new listing if

  • Your company is not yet listed on Aerogela.
  • You represent a manufacturer, distributor, lab, or service provider relevant to the aerogel supply chain.
  • You can provide an official website and verifiable business details.

Use Claim Listing instead if

  • Your company already has a profile on Aerogela.
  • You want to avoid creating a duplicate listing.
  • You need your existing profile linked to an official representative.

What to prepare

  • Official company name and website
  • Core category: producer, distributor, equipment/materials, or research/service
  • Main products and application fields
  • Country/location coverage
  • A short, factual company description
  • A business email on your company domain whenever possible

Editorial review standards

  • The business must be relevant to aerogel materials, equipment, distribution, testing, or R&D services.
  • The website must be live and attributable to a real organization.
  • Marketing claims may be trimmed or rewritten for consistency and clarity.
  • Incomplete, duplicate, or unverifiable submissions may be rejected.

How the process works

  1. Create an account or sign in.
  2. Complete the listing submission form.
  3. Aerogela reviews the submission for fit, quality, and duplication.
  4. Approved listings are published or refined before publication.

Typical review time: 2–5 business days depending on verification complexity.

item.title: Request Quote / Contact Supplier
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Request Quote / Contact Supplier

Use this page to contact a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, laboratory, or service provider listed on Aerogela. For pricing requests, choose Request Quote. For broader business or technical outreach, choose Contact Supplier.

Best practices before you send

  • Identify the product, application, or service you need.
  • Include project timing, target market, and any quantity or sample requirements.
  • Use a valid business email so the supplier or Aerogela team can respond.

If a listing has not yet been officially claimed, Aerogela will review the request and manually route it when appropriate.

item.title: About Aerogela
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
About Aerogela

Aerogela is an editorial directory focused on the global aerogel industry. We organize manufacturers, distributors, equipment suppliers, and research-service providers into searchable listings and landing pages so buyers, engineers, researchers, and business-development teams can discover relevant companies faster.

What Aerogela covers

  • Company listings for producers, distributors, equipment/materials suppliers, and research services.
  • Application and product landing pages for topics such as industrial insulation, EV batteries, cryogenic systems, aerogel blankets, testing, and materials R&D.
  • Directory tools including filtering, compare, claim listing, submit listing, and contact workflows.

What Aerogela is not

  • We are not a manufacturer, trading desk, or certification body.
  • Directory inclusion does not equal endorsement, investment advice, regulatory approval, or a guarantee of commercial performance.
  • Public information can change, so users should confirm fit, pricing, specifications, and compliance directly with the organization before making procurement or technical decisions.

How to use the directory

  1. Browse the main listings directory or a focused landing page.
  2. Use filters to narrow by location, main product, application field, and review status.
  3. Use Compare Listings for side-by-side review.
  4. Use Request Quote / Contact Supplier for outreach.
  5. If you represent a business, use Claim Listing or Submit a Listing.

Trust and directory standards

We publish supporting pages that explain how listings are reviewed, what our verification labels mean, and how to request updates or corrections:

  • How Listings Are Reviewed
  • Verification Policy
  • Editorial Policy

Contact and corrections

If you need to correct a listing, claim a company profile, or request outreach support, please use the published workflows below:

  • Claim Listing
  • Submit a Listing
  • Request Quote / Contact Supplier

item.title: How Listings Are Reviewed
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
How Listings Are Reviewed

Aerogela is an editorial directory. We review listings using publicly available information and selected first-party submissions to improve directory quality, reduce obvious errors, and help users understand the current confidence level of each profile.

Typical review inputs

  • Official company or institution websites
  • Public product, application, or service pages
  • Public contact and location details
  • Claim requests and submit-listing information provided through Aerogela workflows
  • Internal editorial classification of category, main products, and application fields

What we usually check

  • Whether the organization appears active and relevant to the aerogel ecosystem
  • Whether the website and public identity match the listing title
  • Whether the category, location, and core offering look directionally correct
  • Whether the listing needs correction, consolidation, or removal

Review statuses

Reviewed

A Reviewed listing has been checked by Aerogela using editorial review of public information. This means the profile has received a manual quality pass, but it does not mean the business has been independently certified by a third-party authority.

Verified

A Verified listing has stronger confirmation than a standard reviewed profile. In practice this may include a successful claim flow, direct confirmation from the representative, or other higher-confidence validation signals available to the directory.

What review does not guarantee

  • Commercial quality, technical suitability, or pricing competitiveness
  • Regulatory, safety, export-control, or procurement compliance
  • That all information will remain current after publication

Requesting an update

If you represent a listed company and would like to improve or correct a profile, use one of these workflows:

  • Claim Listing
  • Submit a Listing
  • Request Quote / Contact Supplier for communication support

item.title: Verification Policy
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Verification Policy

This page explains what Aerogela means by Verified and how that label differs from standard editorial review.

Meaning of the Verified label

Verified is a directory trust label used to indicate that a listing has received a higher-confidence confirmation signal than a normal editorially reviewed profile.

Possible verification signals

  • An approved Claim Listing workflow tied to the listed organization
  • Direct confirmation from a business representative
  • Matching public business details and internal review records sufficient for stronger confidence

What Verified does not mean

  • It is not a guarantee of product performance, creditworthiness, legal compliance, or business reputation.
  • It is not a substitute for your own technical, procurement, legal, or supplier due diligence.
  • It does not mean Aerogela has audited a factory, laboratory, financial statements, or certifications unless explicitly stated elsewhere.

How a listing may lose verification

  • Claim ownership changes or cannot be maintained
  • Public information materially conflicts with prior verification signals
  • The website or core business identity becomes unclear, inactive, or misleading

How to request verification or correction

If you represent an organization and want to request review, verification, or a correction, start with:

  • Claim Listing
  • Submit a Listing

item.title: Editorial Policy
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Editorial Policy

Aerogela maintains the directory using an editorial process designed to improve discoverability, reduce obvious listing errors, and keep category pages useful for industry research and sourcing.

Editorial principles

  • Relevance: listings should be materially connected to aerogel products, services, research, or the supporting supply chain.
  • Clarity: titles, locations, categories, and website references should reflect the organization as accurately as available public information allows.
  • Conservatism: when evidence is limited, we prefer narrower wording over overstated claims.
  • Correction-friendly: business representatives can request updates through the site workflows.

Sources and editing

We may rely on official websites, public product/service pages, and business-submitted information. Aerogela may standardize wording, categories, and taxonomy labels for consistency across the directory.

Inclusion and removal

  • Listings may be added when they appear relevant to the aerogel ecosystem.
  • Listings may be edited, merged, or removed if they are inactive, misleading, off-topic, duplicate, or no longer useful to directory users.

Commercial neutrality

Directory presence does not imply endorsement. Users should perform their own commercial, technical, regulatory, and supplier due diligence before relying on a listing.

Request an update or contact the directory

  • Claim Listing
  • Submit a Listing
  • Request Quote / Contact Supplier

item.title: What Is Aerogel Insulation? Properties, Uses, and Why It Matters in 2026
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Aerogel insulation is one of the most searched advanced insulation topics in industrial materials, and for good reason. When engineers need very low thermal conductivity, low weight, and high performance in tight spaces, aerogel-based materials often enter the conversation. In simple terms, aerogel is an ultra-porous solid derived from a gel in which the liquid phase is replaced with gas while largely preserving the solid network. The result is a material with extremely low density and excellent thermal insulation behavior.

On Aerogela, we focus on helping buyers, engineers, and researchers discover relevant aerogel companies and products. This guide explains what aerogel insulation is, how it works, and where it is used across energy, industrial, transportation, and construction markets.

What is aerogel insulation?

Aerogel insulation usually refers to thermal insulation products made with silica aerogel or aerogel-enhanced composites. In commercial use, the most common form is aerogel blanket insulation, where a flexible fibrous mat is impregnated with aerogel to create a lightweight insulation product with strong thermal performance.

Other product forms may include boards, panels, particles, powders, and specialty components for thermal management systems. Silica aerogel remains the most widely recognized chemistry because it combines low thermal conductivity with relatively mature manufacturing routes and broad application coverage.

Why aerogel has such low thermal conductivity

Aerogel performs well because of its nanoscale pore structure. The pore network reduces heat transfer through conduction and convection. In practical terms, this means aerogel can often deliver more insulation value per unit thickness than many conventional materials. That advantage matters in applications where space is limited, weight is important, or system temperatures are demanding.

Engineers do not choose aerogel simply because it is a novel material. They choose it when project constraints make thickness, mass, or temperature resistance more important than lowest upfront material cost.

Key properties of aerogel insulation

  • Very low thermal conductivity: useful for thin insulation designs.
  • Light weight: beneficial for transportation, removable covers, and constrained structures.
  • Hydrophobic grades available: some products are designed to resist moisture uptake.
  • Flexible blanket formats: easier installation on pipes, vessels, and complex industrial geometry.
  • Wide application range: suitable for cryogenic and high-temperature thermal systems depending on formulation.

Common applications of aerogel insulation

Aerogel insulation appears in many sectors, especially where energy efficiency and compact design are priorities:

  • Industrial process piping and equipment
  • Oil and gas insulation systems
  • Refining, petrochemical, and LNG facilities
  • Building envelopes and space-constrained retrofit projects
  • EV battery thermal barriers and advanced thermal management assemblies
  • Appliances, transportation, and specialty electronics

Aerogel blanket vs traditional insulation

Compared with mineral wool, foam systems, or other common insulation materials, aerogel blanket products are often selected when the design team cannot simply add more thickness. For example, an industrial pipe rack or retrofit building facade may have limited clearance. In these situations, thinner high-performance insulation can create engineering and maintenance advantages.

That said, aerogel is not automatically the right choice for every project. Total installed cost, operating temperature, mechanical demands, moisture conditions, fire performance requirements, and supply chain reliability all matter.

What buyers should evaluate

If you are sourcing aerogel insulation, compare suppliers on more than headline conductivity data. Useful questions include:

  • Which product form is available: blanket, panel, particle, coating additive, or custom component?
  • What temperature range and test standards are documented?
  • Is the product intended for industrial, building, transportation, or energy-storage use?
  • What certifications, data sheets, and application notes are publicly available?
  • Can the supplier support regional distribution and project-scale volume?

Readers looking for active manufacturers and distributors can browse the Aerogel Producers and Distributors sections on Aerogela.

FAQ: aerogel insulation

Is aerogel insulation the same as silica aerogel?

Not exactly. Silica aerogel is a material family, while aerogel insulation usually refers to usable insulation products built from or enhanced with aerogel.

Where is aerogel insulation used most often?

It is widely discussed in industrial insulation, energy infrastructure, building retrofit, and advanced thermal management applications where thickness and weight are important.

Why is aerogel considered a high-performance insulation material?

Because its porous nanostructure helps reduce heat transfer, allowing strong thermal performance in relatively thin sections.

Final takeaway

Aerogel insulation matters because it solves a real engineering problem: how to achieve strong thermal performance when space, weight, or operating conditions make conventional solutions less attractive. As demand grows in industrial decarbonization, EV thermal safety, and compact construction systems, search interest in aerogel materials is likely to keep increasing. For procurement teams and technical readers, understanding the basics is the first step toward identifying the right suppliers, formats, and application pathways.
item.excerpt:encoded: Learn what aerogel insulation is, how silica aerogel works, where it is used, and why engineers choose it when thermal performance and space efficiency both matter.

item.title: Aerogel Blanket Applications: Oil & Gas, EV Batteries, Construction, and Industrial Insulation
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Aerogel blanket is one of the most commercially important aerogel product formats on the market today. Search demand around aerogel blanket applications continues to rise because project teams want materials that combine thermal performance with installability. A blanket format is easier to wrap, cut, fit, and integrate into real industrial systems than many rigid alternatives.

In this article, we look at the main application sectors where aerogel blanket products are most relevant and why buyers increasingly compare aerogel options when evaluating insulation upgrades.

What is an aerogel blanket?

An aerogel blanket is typically a flexible insulation composite made by integrating aerogel into a fibrous reinforcement matrix. The structure helps deliver low thermal conductivity while maintaining enough flexibility for practical handling and installation. This is especially useful for curved surfaces, removable insulation covers, and retrofit environments where geometry is irregular.

1. Oil and gas insulation

Oil and gas remains one of the best-known application areas for aerogel blanket insulation. Facilities often contain dense process layouts, long pipe runs, valves, vessels, and equipment requiring thermal control. When insulation thickness affects access, weight, or heat retention, aerogel blanket can become attractive.

Common use cases include:

  • Hot process piping
  • Offshore modules where weight matters
  • Subsea or exposed environments depending on system design
  • LNG and cryogenic service in selected insulation architectures

2. Refining and petrochemical plants

Refineries and petrochemical sites often need insulation solutions that balance thermal performance, maintenance access, and long service life. Aerogel blanket may support thinner insulation builds in congested areas while helping reduce heat loss in process systems. Decision-makers usually compare it against mineral wool, calcium silicate, or other established products based on operating temperature, corrosion-under-insulation strategy, and installed system requirements.

3. Industrial insulation and removable covers

Aerogel blanket is frequently discussed for removable insulation pads, turbines, exhaust lines, steam systems, and compact industrial equipment. The blanket format is valuable because it can conform around flanges, valves, and custom housings. For maintenance teams, easier access and reinstallation can matter almost as much as thermal performance.

4. Building envelope and retrofit projects

In construction, aerogel blanket or aerogel-enhanced insulation systems are often evaluated for situations where space is limited. Historic building retrofits, high-value facades, thin wall assemblies, and specialty glazing-adjacent systems are common examples. In these cases, every millimeter matters. A thinner insulation layer can preserve interior space or simplify detailing where bulkier conventional materials create design conflicts.

5. EV battery and thermal management systems

Battery safety and thermal propagation control have pushed more attention toward advanced thermal materials. Aerogel-based barriers and composite formats are now frequently mentioned in EV battery pack discussions. While not every solution is literally a blanket product in the industrial-insulation sense, aerogel-derived flexible thermal barriers are relevant because they combine low conductivity with lightweight integration potential.

For engineers, the important point is not hype but fit-for-purpose design. The right product depends on pack architecture, mechanical requirements, fire-test criteria, manufacturability, and cost targets.

6. Aerospace, rail, marine, and specialty transportation

Transportation sectors care deeply about weight, space, and safety. That makes aerogel blanket and aerogel composite materials interesting for specialty transportation applications ranging from rail systems to marine equipment and aerospace thermal protection concepts. Qualification requirements are strict, but the design logic is consistent: high thermal performance in constrained envelopes.

What makes aerogel blanket attractive across sectors?

  • Thin insulation profiles for tight spaces
  • Reduced weight compared with some traditional systems
  • Flexibility for complex shapes and curved surfaces
  • Potential installation advantages in retrofit work
  • Strong interest in energy efficiency and thermal safety applications

Selection factors before specifying aerogel blanket

Not all aerogel blankets are identical. Before shortlisting a product or supplier, evaluate:

  • Target temperature range
  • Mechanical robustness and compressibility
  • Hydrophobic performance and environmental durability
  • Thickness options and installation method
  • Relevant certifications and application case history
  • Regional supply, lead time, and technical support

If you are comparing supply options, Aerogela’s Aerogel Producers directory is a useful starting point. Buyers looking for channel partners can also review the Distributors directory.

FAQ: aerogel blanket applications

What industries use aerogel blanket most often?

Industrial insulation, oil and gas, refining, construction retrofit, and advanced thermal management are among the most common discussion areas.

Why is aerogel blanket popular in retrofit projects?

Because it can offer strong insulation performance in thinner sections, which is valuable when existing structures leave little room for additional thickness.

Is aerogel blanket only for high-temperature systems?

No. Product suitability depends on the specific formulation and system design. Some applications focus on hot service, while others involve cryogenic or battery-related thermal control.

Conclusion

Aerogel blanket applications continue to expand because the format fits real-world installation needs. It is not simply a laboratory material; it is a practical insulation option for sectors where geometry, thickness, energy efficiency, and safety all matter. As more industries prioritize compact high-performance thermal systems, aerogel blanket will remain a high-intent search topic for engineers, buyers, and technical decision-makers.

item.title: How to Choose Aerogel Suppliers: A Practical B2B Checklist for Engineers and Buyers
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Finding the right aerogel supplier is not the same as finding the cheapest insulation vendor. In many projects, aerogel is selected because the application is constrained, technically demanding, or commercially sensitive. That means supplier selection should go beyond basic marketing claims. Engineers and buyers need a practical evaluation framework.

This guide explains how to compare aerogel suppliers for industrial insulation, thermal management, construction, and specialty materials sourcing. Whether you are searching for silica aerogel blanket, board products, particles, or battery thermal barrier materials, the same sourcing principles apply.

1. Confirm the supplier’s actual product focus

Start by identifying what the company really supplies. Some companies manufacture aerogel materials directly. Others are distributors, converters, or solution providers. That distinction matters for pricing, technical depth, customization, and lead time.

A useful first step is reviewing the supplier landscape by category. Aerogela maintains separate pages for Aerogel Producers and Distributors, which can help buyers narrow the field.

2. Match the product format to the application

Aerogel is not one universal SKU. Buyers should verify whether the supplier offers the right format for the intended use case:

  • Aerogel blanket for industrial insulation and piping
  • Panels or boards for building and engineered assemblies
  • Powders or particles for additives and specialty formulations
  • Thermal barriers or composites for batteries and electronics

If a supplier’s website is vague on product form, ask for a current data sheet and product family overview before moving forward.

3. Review technical data carefully

Conductivity claims alone are not enough. Good supplier evaluation includes:

  • Declared thermal conductivity with test conditions
  • Operating temperature range
  • Density, thickness range, and compression behavior
  • Hydrophobicity or moisture-resistance data
  • Fire, smoke, or other safety-related performance information where relevant

Always ask how the values were measured and under which standards. A realistic, fully documented data package is more valuable than a headline number without context.

4. Look for application evidence, not just product claims

Strong suppliers usually provide evidence that they understand real end-use conditions. This may include case studies, insulation design notes, application engineering support, installation guidance, or sector-specific references. A supplier that can explain how its material behaves in an actual process line, facade assembly, or battery system is usually more useful than one that only posts broad promotional language.

5. Assess supply reliability and geography

For industrial buyers, supply chain reliability is often decisive. Questions worth asking include:

  • Where are the products manufactured?
  • What are standard lead times?
  • Which regions are actively served?
  • Can the supplier support pilot quantities and later scale-up?
  • Is there local technical or distributor support?

This is especially important for multi-site or EPC-managed projects where schedule certainty matters.

6. Ask about certifications and documentation

Depending on the industry, documentation requirements may include SDS files, technical data sheets, quality certifications, compliance declarations, or test reports. Serious suppliers generally make core documents available early in the sales cycle. If documentation is difficult to obtain, that can be a useful signal in itself.

7. Consider total project value, not just unit price

Aerogel products may carry a higher material price than commodity insulation. However, the commercial decision should consider installation thickness, labor implications, transport weight, access constraints, service performance, and maintenance impact. In some projects, the lower-thickness solution creates meaningful lifecycle or system-level value.

8. Build a shortlisting checklist

Before requesting quotations, buyers can use this shortlist framework:

  • Supplier type: producer or distributor
  • Product format matches project need
  • Published data sheets available
  • Relevant technical and compliance documentation available
  • Application references or engineering support evident
  • Regional supply and lead time acceptable
  • Commercial communication responsive and technically credible

FAQ: choosing aerogel suppliers

What is the difference between an aerogel producer and an aerogel distributor?

A producer manufactures the aerogel material or finished product, while a distributor typically resells or represents products within a market or region.

Should buyers prioritize the lowest thermal conductivity?

Not automatically. Buyers should evaluate conductivity together with temperature range, installability, safety, durability, documentation, and supply reliability.

Where can I find aerogel suppliers to compare?

You can start with a structured industry directory such as Aerogela’s listings, then compare the suppliers’ official websites, product documents, and technical positioning.

Final thoughts

Choosing aerogel suppliers is a sourcing exercise that blends materials science, engineering judgment, and procurement discipline. The best supplier is not simply the one with the boldest product claims. It is the one that can document performance, support the target application, and deliver reliably for the scale and region your project demands.

item.title: Silica Aerogel vs Mineral Wool vs PIR: Which Insulation Works Better in Tight Spaces?
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
When project teams compare advanced insulation materials, one of the most common questions is whether silica aerogel is actually better than conventional options such as mineral wool or PIR. The honest answer is: it depends on the project constraint. No single material wins every decision. But when thickness is limited, silica aerogel often becomes much more competitive.

This article offers a practical, SEO-focused comparison for readers searching terms like silica aerogel vs mineral wool, aerogel vs PIR insulation, and high-performance thin insulation materials.

The core difference: thermal performance per thickness

The main reason silica aerogel receives so much attention is that it can offer strong thermal performance in a relatively thin profile. In contrast, mineral wool and PIR are often selected because they are widely available, familiar to contractors, and cost-effective in many standard applications. When enough installation depth is available, conventional materials may be perfectly suitable. When depth is constrained, the economics can change.

Silica aerogel

Silica aerogel is best known for its highly porous nanostructure and very low thermal conductivity. Commercial products are frequently supplied as blankets or composite systems rather than brittle monolithic blocks. The value proposition is clear: reduce thickness while maintaining insulation performance.

Often favored when:

  • Clearance is limited
  • Weight reduction matters
  • Retrofit conditions are difficult
  • Complex geometry needs flexible insulation

Mineral wool

Mineral wool is a widely used insulation material with strong familiarity in industrial and building markets. It is often cost-effective, easy to source, and suitable for many standard thermal and fire-related applications. However, achieving a target insulation value may require more thickness than an aerogel-based system.

Often favored when:

  • Space is less constrained
  • Budgets are highly cost-sensitive
  • The project uses established conventional specifications

PIR insulation

PIR (polyisocyanurate) is common in building insulation and certain panel systems. It is often chosen for its favorable thermal performance relative to some traditional materials and its established role in construction assemblies. However, suitability depends heavily on the specific application, temperature range, code requirements, and system design.

Often favored when:

  • The application is building-focused
  • Panelized or board-type insulation is preferred
  • Project specifications already align with PIR systems

Which insulation is better in tight spaces?

In very tight spaces, silica aerogel often stands out because the design problem is not simply insulation value; it is insulation value within a strict thickness limit. This is common in facade retrofits, industrial equipment enclosures, process lines with access constraints, and specialty thermal management components.

If thickness is not a limiting factor, mineral wool or PIR may remain attractive because of availability and cost structure. But when every millimeter counts, aerogel is far more likely to justify detailed evaluation.

Other buying considerations

  • Installation method and labor requirements
  • Mechanical robustness in actual service
  • Moisture exposure and environmental durability
  • Fire and compliance requirements
  • Availability of technical documentation and local supply

Where to compare suppliers

If your project calls for a thin high-performance insulation material, the next step is supplier comparison rather than theory alone. Aerogela helps users identify companies active in aerogel materials through its Aerogel Producers directory and broader industry listings.

FAQ: aerogel vs conventional insulation

Is silica aerogel always better than mineral wool?

No. It is often more compelling when insulation thickness, weight, or geometry constraints are severe. Mineral wool remains appropriate for many standard applications.

Is PIR a direct substitute for aerogel?

Sometimes the materials may compete in broader thermal design decisions, but they are not interchangeable in every application. Project conditions and system requirements determine suitability.

Why do engineers consider aerogel for retrofit projects?

Because retrofit work often has tight dimensional constraints, and aerogel can help preserve usable space while still improving thermal performance.

Bottom line

The right comparison is not “Which insulation is best in general?” but “Which insulation best fits the project constraint?” Silica aerogel is strongest when tight spaces, difficult geometry, and high thermal performance all matter at the same time. That is why it keeps appearing in high-intent industrial and construction search queries—and why more buyers are actively comparing aerogel suppliers for next-generation insulation projects.

item.title: Aerogel for EV Battery Thermal Runaway Protection: Why Advanced Thermal Barriers Matter
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
EV battery safety has become one of the fastest-growing search topics around advanced thermal materials. Among the materials increasingly discussed in this context, aerogel stands out because it can combine low thermal conductivity with very low weight and compact packaging potential. As battery systems become more energy-dense, the industry focus is shifting from simple heat dissipation to full thermal event management, including resistance to cell-to-cell propagation during thermal runaway scenarios.

This is why phrases such as aerogel for EV batteries, battery thermal runaway barrier, and aerogel thermal insulation for battery packs now attract high-intent engineering and sourcing searches.

Why aerogel is relevant in EV battery systems

Battery pack designers operate under severe constraints: limited space, strict weight targets, manufacturability requirements, and increasing safety expectations. Aerogel-based thermal barriers are attractive because they can help slow heat transfer without adding excessive thickness. In principle, that makes them useful wherever the design team needs a lightweight thermal barrier between cells, modules, or vulnerable components.

Thermal runaway protection and propagation delay

In EV safety discussions, the key question is often not whether a single cell can fail, but whether a thermal event can spread. Materials used inside or around the pack may be selected to delay or reduce thermal propagation, support system compartmentalization, or protect adjacent structures. Aerogel-derived barrier materials are relevant because they can contribute to thermal isolation in compact assemblies.

What buyers should verify

  • Target use: cell spacer, module barrier, pack-level thermal shield, or adjacent component insulation
  • Mechanical integration and manufacturability
  • Thermal performance under the relevant test regime
  • Flame, smoke, and safety-related data where applicable
  • Scalability from prototype to production volume

Why this matters for sourcing

Not every company listed as an aerogel supplier is positioned for EV battery applications. Some focus on industrial insulation, while others address advanced thermal management. Buyers should compare suppliers carefully using public technical information, application focus, and manufacturing credibility. Aerogela’s supplier directory can help identify companies active in this broader ecosystem.

FAQ

Is aerogel used directly inside EV batteries?

Use cases vary by product design. In many discussions, aerogel appears as part of a thermal barrier or insulation layer within the broader pack architecture.

Why not just use thicker conventional insulation?

Because EV packs are highly space-constrained, and every added millimeter affects packaging, energy density, and manufacturability.

How should buyers shortlist suppliers?

Compare application focus, technical literature, manufacturability support, and evidence of battery-related use cases.

item.title: Aerogel Insulation and CUI Risk: Why Hydrophobic Materials Matter in Industrial Systems
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Corrosion under insulation, commonly called CUI, is a major lifecycle concern in industrial facilities. Whenever insulated piping and equipment are exposed to moisture ingress, the hidden corrosion risk can create safety, maintenance, and cost problems. This is one reason buyers increasingly search for information about aerogel insulation and CUI, especially in process industries, refining, and offshore environments.

Why CUI matters

CUI is difficult because it often develops beneath the insulation system where direct visual inspection is limited. Material choice alone does not eliminate the problem, but insulation design, moisture behavior, cladding quality, maintenance strategy, and operating conditions all influence risk.

Why aerogel enters the discussion

Some aerogel insulation products are promoted as hydrophobic or moisture-resistant, which is relevant in CUI conversations. In practical terms, buyers want to know whether the insulation system can reduce water retention, support faster drying, or otherwise fit a lower-risk insulation strategy. These are application-specific questions, so public claims should always be checked against product documentation.

What to evaluate in supplier documentation

  • Hydrophobic performance claims and test methods
  • Service temperature range
  • System design recommendations for jacketing and sealing
  • Installation guidance and maintenance considerations
  • Industrial case references where available

Aerogel is not a standalone CUI cure

It is important to avoid oversimplification. No insulation material alone guarantees zero CUI. Good engineering still requires proper weather barriers, installation quality, inspection planning, and corrosion management. However, hydrophobic aerogel blanket products are relevant because they may fit strategies aimed at reducing moisture-related performance concerns in challenging industrial settings.

Related supplier research

If your team is comparing industrial insulation suppliers, start with Aerogela’s Aerogel Producers section, then check each company’s official technical literature for hydrophobicity and industrial service data.

FAQ

Does aerogel eliminate CUI risk entirely?

No. It may support a lower-risk system strategy, but design, cladding, and maintenance still matter.

Why is hydrophobic behavior important here?

Because moisture management strongly affects insulation reliability and corrosion-related maintenance concerns.

What should buyers ask suppliers first?

Ask for hydrophobicity data, system recommendations, and industrial-use documentation.

item.title: Aerogel for Cryogenic Insulation: LNG, Cold Storage, and Low-Temperature System Design
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Aerogel is often associated with high-performance industrial insulation, but it is also highly relevant in low-temperature and cryogenic discussions. Search interest around aerogel for cryogenic insulation continues to grow because LNG infrastructure, cold-chain systems, and low-temperature process equipment all demand careful control of heat transfer, thickness, and reliability.

Why cryogenic insulation is challenging

Cryogenic systems operate under conditions where heat ingress must be minimized and insulation design errors can become expensive very quickly. Storage tanks, transfer lines, valves, and associated equipment all need insulation strategies that support efficiency, frost control, and long-term performance.

Why aerogel is relevant

Aerogel-based insulation can be attractive in cryogenic contexts because it is associated with low thermal conductivity and compact insulation design. In systems where space, weight, or complex geometry matter, thinner high-performance insulation can offer practical engineering value.

Typical cryogenic and low-temperature use cases

  • LNG and gas-processing infrastructure
  • Cold storage and specialty process equipment
  • Low-temperature industrial piping
  • Equipment with limited clearance for thick insulation systems

Key evaluation criteria

  • Thermal performance at relevant low-temperature conditions
  • Mechanical handling and installability
  • Moisture behavior in low-temperature environments
  • Compatibility with the broader insulation system design
  • Available case history and technical support

For buyer teams, the real task is not simply finding a product with a strong conductivity number. It is finding a supplier that can document low-temperature fit and support the required system design. Aerogela’s industry directory can help narrow the search.

FAQ

Is aerogel only used in high-temperature systems?

No. It is also highly relevant in cryogenic and low-temperature insulation discussions.

Why does aerogel attract LNG-related interest?

Because compact, high-performance insulation is valuable in demanding low-temperature infrastructure.

What should buyers verify?

Low-temperature test context, system fit, and supplier support for cryogenic applications.

item.title: Thin Insulation for Building Retrofit: Where Aerogel Can Outperform Bulkier Materials
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
Building retrofit projects often face a basic conflict: improve thermal performance without sacrificing too much interior space or disrupting existing architectural constraints. This is exactly why thin insulation building retrofit has become an important search topic—and why aerogel-based insulation products are regularly part of the conversation.

Why retrofit projects are different

In new construction, designers may have more freedom to allocate wall thickness. In retrofit work, especially in dense urban buildings or historically sensitive structures, space is limited. Even small increases in insulation thickness can affect window details, room dimensions, service penetrations, or facade geometry.

Where aerogel fits

Aerogel is attractive in retrofit contexts because it is associated with strong thermal performance in thin sections. That makes it relevant for wall upgrades, specialty interior insulation layers, facade details, and other locations where conventional bulkier insulation may be difficult to use.

What project teams should compare

  • Required thermal performance versus available thickness
  • Moisture management and building-physics implications
  • Fire, code, and assembly requirements
  • Installation complexity and labor considerations
  • Total value of preserved usable space

Why this topic matters for SEO

People searching this topic are often not casual readers. They are architects, specifiers, retrofit consultants, and product researchers looking for a solution to a specific design constraint. That makes aerogel retrofit content especially useful for attracting high-intent organic traffic.

Readers who want to explore relevant materials suppliers can continue through Aerogela’s producer listings and broader blog archive.

FAQ

Why is aerogel relevant in retrofit projects?

Because retrofit work often has strict thickness constraints and aerogel can provide strong insulation performance in thin sections.

Is aerogel a universal replacement for standard building insulation?

No. It is most compelling when space preservation is a major part of the project value.

Who typically searches this topic?

Architects, specifiers, retrofit consultants, and buyers evaluating thin high-performance insulation options.

item.title: Aerogel Insulation Price: What Actually Drives Cost in Industrial and Commercial Projects?
item.dc:creator: aerogelaadmin
item.content:encoded:
One of the most common commercial questions in the aerogel industry is simple: why is aerogel insulation expensive, and when is the cost justified? Buyers searching aerogel insulation price are usually comparing more than a material quote. They are trying to understand whether a thinner, higher-performance insulation system creates enough project value to offset a higher upfront cost.

Why aerogel insulation price is different from commodity insulation

Aerogel is usually chosen when project constraints are demanding. That means price should be evaluated in the context of thickness limits, operating temperature, labor access, geometry complexity, and lifecycle impact. Comparing aerogel directly against a low-cost commodity insulation by square-meter material price alone can be misleading.

Main factors that influence aerogel insulation cost

  • Product format such as blanket, panel, particle, or engineered thermal barrier
  • Thickness and density specification
  • Application temperature range and performance requirements
  • Volume purchased and regional supply chain availability
  • Whether the source is a producer or distributor
  • Installation complexity in the real project environment

When higher price can still make economic sense

Aerogel can become commercially attractive when thinner insulation reduces rework, preserves interior space, simplifies retrofit design, reduces weight, or lowers labor time around complex geometry. Product specification and application context. Format, thickness, temperature requirements, and order volume all matter.
